stimulus.title: The Scratchy C-String
stimulus.body: On the Tuesday I brought home my rented three-quarter violin, I imagined I would sound like a concert soloist by Friday. Instead, my first draw of the bow produced a sound somewhere between a rusty gate and an indignant magpie. My teacher, Mrs Kovács, did not wince. She simply tapped the music stand with her pencil and said, 'Good. You made a sound. Now let us teach your right elbow to breathe.' For the first month, I was not allowed to play a single tune—only long, slow open strings while watching my bow hair track parallel to the bridge in a full-length mirror. It felt absurdly slow when my friends in band were already marching through film themes. Yet six months later, when we finally tackled a crisp folk dance, my bow stayed steady while faster learners skidded across the strings. Looking back, Mrs Kovács's stubbornness taught me something larger than music: rushing past the foundations only borrows speed you will have to pay back later.

workedSolution: The narrator says: 'For the first month, I was not allowed to play a single tune—only long, slow open strings.'

reviewFocus: Verify passage evidence, Australian English, and absence of defensible distractor readings.

The padlock had been broken with a heavy hammer.

stimulus.title: The Missing Brass Compass
stimulus.body: When the Year 6 orienteering trophies were packed into the sports shed on Friday afternoon, Mr Henderson locked the padlock and slipped the key into his whistle lanyard. By Monday morning, the padlock hung open, and the antique brass compass donated by the local bushwalking club was gone from its velvet box. Yet nothing else had been touched—not the new mountain bikes, not the cricket kits, not even the digital stopwatches. Sienna, who was helping Mr Henderson sweep the gravel path outside, noticed two faint, muddy footprints leading away from the shed door toward the oval. Beside the second print lay a small, torn corner of blue-lined graph paper with the numbers '045° — 32 paces' scribbled in pencil. Sienna frowned. No burglar chasing valuable equipment would leave behind mountain bikes and stopwatches just to take a compass—and then pace out bearings across the school oval.

reviewFocus: Verify passage evidence, Australian English, and absence of defensible distractor readings.
